scope: Old Greek Daniel in Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending.
historical_records: Existing index and reference records were consulted as historical reference, not proof of fresh complete Greek verification.

chapters.title: Daniel 1
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary address and the giving request at 1:12–13; legumes makes the food sense plain while retaining earth, ten days and water. Preserve Abiesdri as chief eunuch and the direct agent of the trial, the royal names, the three years, and the expanded education and appointment account at 1:20. Historical notes using pulse remain preserved.

chapters.title: Daniel 2
chapters.decision: Distinguish ordinary royal address from the direct prayer to God at 2:23, where Thee/Thou hast remain. Smooth Arioch’s introduction and the image’s appearance, preserving chief cook, the angel in 2:11, the difficult dwelling clause in 2:22, the stone that struck the whole earth in 2:35, iron cutting every tree, and the separate kingdom wording in 2:44. Keep the expanded list including fish of the sea and the source’s repeated last-days phrases.

chapters.title: Daniel 3
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary royal address and third-person verbs while retaining Thou/Thee/Thy and matching verbs throughout direct prayer to God. Retain the full prayer and song, every repeated blessing, the eighteenth year, India-to-Ethiopia scope, measurements and instruments, repeated sevenfold heat, hand-and-foot binding and the forty-nine-cubit flame. Preserve the confident reply at 3:18 and angel of God at 3:92. The difficult repeated behind Thee clauses at 3:40 remain unresolved rather than replaced from another textual form.

chapters.title: Daniel 4
chapters.decision: Modernize address to the king and third-person verbs, repair is thou at 4:20, and distinguish the quotation boundaries as the account shifts between first-person report and third-person narration. Preserve the repeated tree appearance, thirty-stadia branches, sun and moon, the shift from tree to his body, seven years, custody and bronze bonds, the Temple-destruction statement, redeem/almsgiving, the replacement ruler and all lettered units. Render the present are rushing at 4:24 rather than silently treating it as future.

chapters.title: Daniel 5
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary royal address and verbs, preserve the unnumbered preface as a distinct anchored reading unit, and close Daniel’s speech after the combined 5:26–28 unit. Retain the two thousand guests in the preface, its Mane/Phares/Thekel sequence distinct from 5:17, the queen’s summons, authority over a third part, the grouped labels and gaps, and the ending that reports transfer of kingship without adding the king’s death.

chapters.title: Daniel 6
chapters.decision: Repair did thou and Before thou, modernize ordinary address and third-person verbs, and smooth the sealed-pit and assembled-forces clauses. Preserve Artaxerxes/Darius in the opening, 127 satraps, two accusers, repeated three daily prayers and the thirty-day restriction, Daniel’s direct rebuke to the king, divine care closing the lions’ mouths, the deaths of the accusers with their families and the final succession notice.

chapters.title: Daniel 7
chapters.decision: Retain the already natural wording through most of this chapter and smooth its closing time phrase. Preserve the lioness, a tongue given to the leopard, plans in the horns, three horns withering, watching the sound, and the source’s as an Ancient of Days at 7:13. Keep the unusual worship list, four kingdoms that will perish, the time/times/half-time period and the past gave at 7:27. No familiar-version substitutions or doctrinal glosses were added.

chapters.title: Daniel 9
chapters.decision: Keep direct prayer in Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine with matching verbs, while using modern third-person belongs/has and ordinary you in Gabriel’s address. Preserve the prayer’s shifts between addressing God and speaking of Him, singular servant and plural servants, the city and people names, seventy weeks, gladdening a holy of holies, and the exact differing number formulas at 9:26–27. No chronology or familiar anointing formula was supplied.

chapters.title: Daniel 11
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary address and third-person verbs, open the renewed speech at 11:2, and clarify the carried-over clause and so will his son at 11:10 without moving its verse boundary. Preserve Egypt/north designations, all repeated roots, plant and arm images, the Romans at 11:30, my country at 11:41, and the clauses continuing across 11:28–29 and 11:38–39. No historical identities are inserted into the Scripture.

chapters.title: Susanna
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary address and third-person verbs while retaining who knowest/Thou knowest in Susanna’s prayer. Repair thee who hast and preserve Listen, listen, the repeated soul in the mastic-tree exchange, and you both followed by singular you in 1:59. Smooth the beauty/filthy-desire clause and reflect the repeated releasing of guilty people. Preserve the source start at 1:6, every gap/grouped label, five hundred servants, four children, the angel giving understanding, ravine and fire judgment and the final praise of the young.

chapters.title: Bel and the Dragon
chapters.decision: Modernize ordinary address and third-person verbs and retain the separation between Daniel’s speech and the narrator’s seventy-priests statement in 1:9. Preserve the Habakkuk/Joshua/Levi heading, Daniel as priest and son of Abal, all food quantities and units, seventy priests apart from families, the ashes and seals, thirty minas of pitch, seven lions, two daily bodies, six days, Habakkuk’s meal and return, and the repeated divine remembrance. Keep plural address to the priests and singular address to the king distinguishable through their named addressees at 1:15–17.
